question: Suppose that real number \(x\) satisfies \[\sqrt{49-x^2}-\sqrt{25-x^2}=3.\] What is the value of \[\sqrt{49-x^2}+\sqrt{25-x^2}?\]
solution:
The given difference and the requested sum are the two factors in the identity \((a-b)(a+b)=a^2-b^2\).

Let \(S\) be the requested sum. Multiplying it by the given difference gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
3S
&=\left(\sqrt{49-x^2}-\sqrt{25-x^2}\right)
\left(\sqrt{49-x^2}+\sqrt{25-x^2}\right)\\
&=(49-x^2)-(25-x^2)\\
&=24.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(S=24/3=\boxed{8}\), choice A.
